Event: `39236914cfaf82b9ad171b88e6e89cd8` · 2026-09-24T23:24:22Z

> K6 PLAN v1 REVIEW (red team). VERDICT: BLOCK, on two P1s. Both are about the test fixture's design, not the deletion itself; a v2 that answers them plus the P2s below is likely OK. The kernel inventory, OD1, OD3, OD4, OD6 and OD8 are sound. Read at wp-k5 30d984ffb, with the K5b plan. Nothing was edited.
> 
> [1/3] P1s
> 
> P1-1. The rendezvous after SIDs is not designed. Today every multi-party case meets through well-known SIDs: checker::ADDRESS, victim::ADDRESS (budget-*), mem-victim, uaf-holder, return-lent-borrower and move-borrowed. After K6 the boot wiring has exactly two endpoints: the boot endpoint, whose receive right goes to the 2nd program, and the log endpoint, whose receive right goes to the 1st. But uaf-lent-page, mem-attack, return-lent-unmapped, lend-untouched, touch-beyond-ram and the five budget-* attack cases each need two servers among the non-first programs (a victim or holder, plus attack-checker). The plan only says 'handles: boot and log endpoints now; process_start lists, mint' and 'the checker powers off through log-server'. That leaves unsaid how checker::done() reaches the checker, and how an attacker sends GO to a budget-victim. Needed in v2, as a per-case table: the program order; who holds the boot receive right (it can mint any badge on that endpoint, so say whether it may be the attacker); and each old SID's replacement. Recommendation: fold the checker into log-server as a DONE op, printing a fixed template with the reporter's badge and then calling system_reset. Put the single victim or holder server 2nd, with clients calling it on the boot endpoint. Explicitly forbid a REGISTER/LOOKUP name broker in log-server: that is the name lookup (TOFU) K6 deletes, rebuilt in userspace.
> 
> P1-2. 'log-server first everywhere' conflicts with cases whose first program must hold the device objects, and the OD2(c) list misses them:
> - timeouts and timeouts-tcg: the first program receives on a device IRQ handle, and log-server is 2nd on the legacy grant;
> - budget-destroy-kills (budget-destroy-system, log-server, budget-victim): not an attack case and not in (c);
> - K5b's APPROVED plan makes virtio-probe FIRST in bench-virtio-devices, 'keeps logging through log-server', and has 'the orchestrator P (the first program)' in dma-reset-quarantine. dma-rules and dma-reset-attack likewise use the first program's devices.
> After K6, log-server can print only when it is first, since the UART grant fallback is gone. So each of these needs OD2(c), direct console, or a stated hand-off. The plan's Devices row ('virtio-probe: power-off through log-server') contradicts K5b. Put every case in v2's table, with its order.

### K6 red team · Reply

Event: `98383a5f68d7fb5e013b4acdded21467` · 2026-09-24T23:24:22Z

> [2/3] P2s
> 
> P2-1. The Yield inventory is incomplete. lib.rs wait_ms() also calls yield_slice. It is used by budget-carve-attack, budget-destroy-system, budget-mem-churn, budget-table-attack, budget-test, ipc-outcomes, and rd.rs's Busy retries (rd.rs:265 and :275). And park() is the panic handler of all about 55 programs, plus sched.rs's 7 calls. Say what wait_ms becomes: receive(None, timeout) changes timing in the budget and ipc-outcomes cases.
> 
> P2-2. Putting the log handle in slot 2 silently changes existing Redoubt negative tests:
> - redoubt-attack.rs:46 has mint_from_handle(2,1,None), commented 'handles this program does not hold', and :49 has Some(2), 'a budget it does not hold'.
> - With OD2, index 2 is a badged log handle, so the rows would test NotPermitted or a wrong-type error, not a missing handle. Re-recording the expected line would weaken the I3/I4 coverage.
> - Use first_free() or u32::MAX-1 in those rows, and audit every literal index in non-first programs. Do both in commit 1.
> 
> P2-3. TAKE_BUDGETS 'moves' root, system and users, but KERNEL-SPEC:163 says message handles are COPIED ('the sender keeps its own'). log-server must handle_close its copies after replying, or it keeps root through every budget attack. It should also print a fixed '[server] budgets given to pid N' line that the cases expect, because first-come is ordering, not authority.
> 
> P2-4. POWEROFF widens who can power off. Before, only the checker could, through its grant, so a clean power-off was evidence in itself. Now any holder of a log handle can. The defence then rests on every poweroff=true case expecting the checker's line. Make it structural: for poweroff=true, the testbench requires the server's power-off line naming the declared checker PID and fails on any other PID. Also check that SBI system_reset gives the same QEMU exit status as the 0x5555 write (poweroff_status).
> 
> P2-5. legacy-gone is necessary, not sufficient. Proposed additions:
> (a) A static gate: a bench check that the kernel, loader, libs and tests/programs contain no SysCall, rsyscall, RETURN_FROM_ISR, in_callback, PREVIOUS_PAIR, HANDLING_IRQ, connection_map, SID/CID, Grnt or create_server. Build the kernel with warnings denied, so orphaned legacy helpers cannot survive. Examples: arch/riscv/mem.rs's lend_page_inner, move_page_inner, hand_page_to_user, update_page_flags and page_is_lent, none of which the plan lists; and ppid.
> (b) Sweep a0 = NUMBER_BASE and the last Redoubt number + 1, and on rv64 also n|1<<32 and n|1<<63.
> (c) Observable post-conditions:
> - MapMemory rows pass a fixed virt, and map_fixed there must succeed afterwards;
> - ClaimInterrupt(10, cb), with cb setting a flag: after the [[input]] echo the flag is still unset.
> (d) A recorded negative run: legacy-gone FAILS on 7c, the parent of 7d.

> R1 (P2). In C, dma-reset-attack's P mints badges for its spawn.rs children, and logsrv relays badge N as '[pid N]'. The adversarial child there is the reuse process. If P ever mints badge 2, which is its own PID, that child's relayed lines become '[pid 2] ...' lines, byte-identical to P's own verdict lines. Required: minted badges come from a range disjoint from bundle PIDs (>= 0x100, since PIDs are <= 64), or logsrv relays minted badges as '[badge N]'. Also state that C's 'no adversary' means 'the first program is the trusted tester'. proc-attack, map-fixed-attack, write-only-attack and pid-reuse-authority are first-and-alone self-checking negative tests, which is fine but conflicts with the rule's literal text.

### K6 red team · Reply

Event: `5caea5229b29be7a6aa5916d2ed95955` · 2026-09-24T23:42:44Z

> [2/2] The Error fold, the no-cruft gate, the numbers
> 
> N1 (must adopt). The Error fold into redoubt_sys::Error. No user-visible value can change through the legacy path: after 7d no legacy Error reaches a register, and the model and sys host tests never see kernel-internal errors. The risk is the boundary, in two places.
> 
> (a) arch/riscv/mem.rs:860 address_available() is virt_to_phys(v).is_err_and(|e| e == BadAddress). It depends on checked_phys telling an empty PTE (BadAddress) from a reservation (MemoryInUse) and a lent page (ShareViolation). find_virtual_address (mem.rs:409 and :427) uses it for map_anon's placement. Collapse those three into one sys variant and a lent page in the 0x6000_0000 window reads as free. map_page_in then refuses it (is_occupied sees S), and map_anon returns OutOfMemory to a process that only has a lend open. That is a silent user-visible error change. Also note that is_occupied does not cover reservations, so only address_available keeps a map from landing on one.
> 
> (b) Today every Redoubt path reaches the legacy error layer through an explicit mapping, because the two types differ: message.rs:488/777/778/1062/1232/1236/1338, process.rs:298/305/346, redoubt.rs:226 and mem.rs:276/1166/1240. After the fold the types match, so a bare ? compiles and would leak OutOfMemory where the spec says InvalidArgument; message.rs:777 is an example. can_return only checks that an error is in the row, not that it is the right one, and it runs only in debug builds.
> 
> Required wording:
> 1. The page layer (arch/riscv/mem.rs and mem.rs's frame and PTE functions) keeps a module-private enum. It is named in the plan, with Unmapped, Reserved, Lent, NoFrame and NonCanonical or similar. address_available tests the PTE directly.
> 2. redoubt_sys::Error appears only at and above those boundaries.
> 3. 8b's review checks every listed map_err/ok_or site byte for byte, and no new ? crosses the boundary.
> 4. redoubt_sys::Error gains no variant.
> 
> N2 (must adopt). As specified, the no-cruft gate fails on K6's own required code:
> - The kernel must contain 'Grnt' to panic on it, and legacy-gone.rs and its toml name ClaimInterrupt, RETURN_FROM_ISR and friends. The gate's own pattern list sits in tools/testbench or tests/ and matches itself. Give it an explicit allowlist: those three paths, or a spelling such as b"Grn\x74".
> - 'more than one const PAGE_SIZE|PAGE|USER_AREA_END': OD9 itself defines USER_AREA_END twice (rv32 and rv64). tests/programs has 'const PAGE' in map-fixed-attack, map-fixed-tables, proc-attack, write-only-attack, stub-launch and spawn.rs; stub/fuzz has its own. Count only literal-valued definitions, treat a per-width pair as one, and remove or allow the aliases.
> - 'Cargo feature without a cfg user': qemu-virt has 0 cfg users. It is a board alias the bench's target.rs selects. Exempt features that only enable other features.
> - Make only \bxous\b case-insensitive. With -i, SysCall matches redoubt_sys::syscall across rt and sys; I dry-ran it. Case-sensitive, on the untouched dirs it hits only the expected files: sys call.rs and tests.rs, loader and grants.
> - Cruft the sweep misses: .cargo/config.toml's '--cfg crossbeam_no_atomic_64' (for hosted crossbeam), the baremetal cfg itself with its build.rs and check-cfg entry once OD1 makes everything unconditional, cfg(ci), the unsafe-budget.toml 'Xous' comment, 15 'legacy' mentions in tests/*.toml, and loader dt.rs:216's 'legacy claim path'.
> 
> Numbers: consistent. The unsafe count is 52 at the tip, and -6 (server.rs, hosted return_memory, memory_range, the bzero call and declaration, from_raw) plus K5b's +2 gives about 48, within <= 50. Layout goes to 0 under forbid(unsafe). About 11,300 lines matches §2's arithmetic. The always-created log endpoint page moves no exact accounting: every system usage check I found is relative (budget-test, budget-table-attack, budget-mem-churn, device-test, ipc-outcomes). OD9 is fine; pick the width by target_pointer_width, so host crates get rv64.

> The red team re-reviewed v2: OK WITH NOTES, and the BLOCK is lifted. Fold these into the plan file in place (the final version for the owner), post a short disposition on K6-plan, then complete the assignment. Still PLAN ONLY.
> R1 (P2): logsrv relays minted badges as '[pid N]', so an adversarial child with minted badge 2 can forge P's own '[pid 2]' verdict lines. Minted badges must be >= 0x100 (never overlapping PIDs), AND/OR relayed with a distinct prefix ('[badge N]'). Do both if cheap. Add a forgery case.
> R2: TAKE_GIFTS never hands out DMA-capable virtio devices.
> R3: anchor the DONE rule (only the checker's DONE counts, and the bench matches it anchored), and add a forged DONE to the forgery case.
> N1 (must adopt), my ruling: the Error fold is allowed only at the syscall boundary. The page/mem layer keeps a named private enum (address_available's BadAddress vs MemoryInUse/ShareViolation distinction must survive; otherwise map_anon returns OutOfMemory while a lend is open). redoubt_sys::Error is used only at the boundary, with every listed map_err site explicit (no bare ?). Commit 8b's review checks each site against KERNEL-SPEC's Errors rows. No new sys variant, and no user-visible error value, order or meaning changes. This still meets the owner's one-definition rule: the private enum is kernel-internal, not a duplicate of a user-visible type.
> N2 (must adopt): fix the no-cruft gate so it doesn't trip on K6's own intentional code. Allowlist the kernel's Grnt refusal, the legacy-gone sources and the gate's own patterns. Resolve OD9's duplicate USER_AREA_END and the 'const PAGE' aliases (ONE definition). Remove or justify qemu-virt with no cfg user. Make only 'xous' case-insensitive. Extend the sweep to the crossbeam cfg flag, the baremetal cfg and build.rs, and the legacy wording in tomls and loader/dt.rs.
> The owner reviews the plan next.
